definition: Region-based Convolutional Neural Networks (R-CNN) are a family of machine learning models for computer vision, and specifically object detection and localization.
details: The original goal of R-CNN was to take an input image and produce a set of bounding boxes as output, where each bounding box contains an object and also the category (e.g. car or pedestrian) of the object. In general, R-CNN architectures perform selective search over feature maps outputted by a CNN. R-CNN has been extended to perform other computer vision tasks, such as: tracking objects from a drone-mounted camera, locating text in an image, and enabling object detection in Google Lens. Mask R-CNN is also one of seven tasks in the MLPerf Training Benchmark, which is a competition to speed up the training of neural networks.

explainer.lead: A family of computer vision models for object detection and localization. It matters because it produces bounding boxes with object categories from an input image.

tiers.eli5: It's like drawing boxes around every object in a photo and writing the object's name next to each box.
tiers.practitioner: Architectures perform selective search over feature maps outputted by a CNN, extended to tasks like tracking from drone-mounted cameras, locating text, and object detection in Google Lens; a pitfall is that the search step adds cost beyond plain classification.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as taking an input image and producing a set of bounding boxes, each containing an object and its category; in general, R-CNN architectures perform selective search over feature maps outputted by a CNN. Extensions include Mask R-CNN.

explainer.example: Given a photo, the model outputs a box around a car labeled 'car' and a box around a pedestrian labeled 'pedestrian'.
